content: The initial dosage of cycloserine is 250 mg taken orally every 12 hours for 14 days. After this, the maintenance dosage is adjusted to 500 mg to 1 g per day, divided into doses every 12 hours, for a duration of 18 to 24 months. The total daily dose should not exceed 1 g. Blood levels of the drug should be monitored regularly. For patients with renal impairment, the dosing interval should be adjusted based on creatinine clearance (CrCl): CrCl 50–80 mL/min: Administer every 12–16 hours. CrCl 10–49 mL/min: Administer every 24–36 hours. CrCl <10 mL/min: Administer every 36–48 hours. Cycloserine is part of a multi-drug regimen and is not considered a first-line treatment. It is typically used in combination with other medications to treat tuberculosis (TB) and, in some cases, urinary tract infections (UTIs). It is effective only against bacterial infections and does not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu. To achieve the best therapeutic effect, the medication should be taken at evenly spaced intervals, and the full prescribed course should be completed, even if symptoms improve. Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) may be prescribed alongside cycloserine to prevent certain side effects. Drug Interactions: 1. Ethionamide and Cycloserine: These drugs can increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to enhanced central nervous system (CNS) toxicity and an increased risk of seizures. Use with caution and monitor closely. 2. Isoniazid and Cycloserine: Isoniazid can increase the toxicity of cycloserine by reducing its metabolism, which may also enhance CNS toxicity and the risk of seizures. Use with caution and monitor closely. 3. Cycloserine and Sodium Picosulfate/Magnesium Oxide/Anhydrous Citric Acid: Cycloserine may reduce the effectiveness of these agents by altering their metabolism. Co-administration with antibiotics may further decrease efficacy by disrupting colonic bacterial flora necessary for drug activation. Monitor closely. Side Effects: Common side effects include headache, drowsiness, dizziness, and tremors. Serious side effects may include confusion, restlessness, vertigo, cardiac arrhythmias, folate deficiency, hyperreflexia, dysarthria, coma, increased liver enzymes, somnolence, paresis, seizures, heart failure, and hypersensitivity reactions. CNS toxicity, including depression, psychosis, and seizures, may occur. Prolonged use can lead to fungal or bacterial superinfections, such as Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea. Contraindications and Precautions: Avoid use in patients with severe renal dysfunction, a history of seizure disorders, severe mental health conditions (e.g., depression, anxiety, psychosis), or alcoholism, as these conditions may increase the risk of seizures. Use with caution in patients with anemia or impaired hepatic or renal function. Cycloserine may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Avoid alcohol and marijuana, as they can exacerbate these effects. Do not drive or operate machinery until you are sure you can do so safely. Live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine) may not work effectively during cycloserine treatment. Pregnancy and Lactation: Pregnancy Category C: Use only if clearly needed, as there is insufficient evidence to confirm safety during pregnancy. Lactation: Cycloserine passes into breast milk but is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Pharmacokinetics: Mechanism of Action: Cycloserine is bacteriostatic or bactericidal, inhibiting bacterial cell wall synthesis. Absorption: 70–90%. Metabolism: Primarily hepatic. Half-life: Approximately 10 hours in patients with normal renal function. Peak plasma levels: Achieved within 4–8 hours. Excretion: 60–70% excreted unchanged in urine. Overdose: In the event of an overdose, symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing require immediate medical attention. In the U.S., contact poison control at 1-800-222-1222. In Canada, call 1-844-764-7669. Monitoring: Regular laboratory tests, including sputum tests, cycloserine blood levels, kidney and liver function tests, and complete blood counts, are recommended during treatment. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. Storage: Store at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or unused medication as instructed by your healthcare provider. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into drains unless directed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about cycloserine. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
